title: Response Length Perception and Sequence Scheduling: An LLM-Empowered LLM Inference Pipeline
technique: LLM-based response-length prediction (instruction-tuned) + length-grouped micro-batching with failure re-collection and variable batch size

optimized_metrics.evidence: This approach intelligently groups queries with similar response lengths, reducing computational waste and improving inference throughput without compromising performance.
This approach intelligently groups queries with similar response lengths, reducing computational waste and improving inference throughput without compromising performance.

headline_claim.text: an impressive 86% improvement in inference throughput compared to the vanilla batch inference without compromising effectiveness

reported_metrics.where: Tables 4-6 (mean generated length per batch, redundant computation)

metric_definitions.definition_quote: We evaluate the throughput at the sample level and report the number of samples processed per second and the corresponding improvement compared to the vanilla baseline, where inference is conducted with batch size 16.
metric_definitions.notes: offline sample-level throughput (requests/s), not token throughput; baseline is vanilla batch size 16

metric_definitions.definition_quote: The average length refers to the mean length of each batch, where a smaller average length indicates reduced redundant computation.

the metric Error(w), which measures the difference between the estimated number of words and the actual word number. We also consider two thresholds for accuracy: Acc-50 and Acc-100, where a prediction is considered correct if the difference falls below 50 and 100 words, respectively.
metric_definitions.notes: length prediction measured in words, not tokens

load_regime: offline batch inference (10,000 alpaca prompts; Instruction-in-Wild dataset), group size 256, no arrival process
tradeoff_acknowledged: mispredicted (too short) lengths cause failure re-collection and recomputation; mean-length prediction raises failure ratio to 29.8% and gain drops to 45%; larger batches for short responses constrained by memory
models: Vicuna-7B (LLaMA-based); length predictors: GPT-4, Claude, ChatGPT, Vicuna variants
extractor_notes: Offline throughput only: no latency, TTFT, TPOT or SLOs at all.
